title: macOS blackboxd/bro-harness redeploy (stablesign + launchd)
content: Redeploy signing now uses the operator's stablesign helper (shell alias `stablesign`) instead of ad-hoc `codesign -f -s -`: it signs with a persistent self-signed codesigning identity from the login keychain, so the designated requirement is stable across binary swaps. Consequences: TCC privacy grants (notably network volumes - an invalidated grant makes daemon-spawned git/fs calls on automounts hang silently, wedging the IndexWriterActor) and launchd's cached LWCR both survive redeploys. Flow: back up prior binary to `.bak` -> cp new binary into ~/.local/bin -> `stablesign ~/.local/bin/blackboxd` -> `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.daystrom.blackbox` (bootout/bootstrap dance only as fallback if kickstart still refuses) -> verify port 7264 responds. If indexing goes quiet after any signing change, check System Settings for a pending TCC consent. Note KeepAlive{SuccessfulExit:false}: a clean exit 0 will NOT be auto-restarted. The daemon links bro-harness/bro-tools in-process, so rebuilding blackboxd captures library-crate changes; rebuild + stablesign the standalone bro-harness bin too for consistency.
